questions.stem: Where can a company download AWS compliance reports, such as SOC and ISO reports, to share with its auditors?

options.rationale: Security Hub brings together and prioritizes security findings about your own accounts; it does not provide AWS's audit reports.
AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance reports and agreements.
Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities.

questions.explanation: The clue is reports about AWS itself, such as SOC and ISO reports, to hand to auditors: AWS Artifact provides these on demand. Security Hub and AWS Config check your own resources, not AWS's.

questions.stem: A company must keep a long-term record of all AWS API activity in its account for security investigations. Where should it have AWS CloudTrail deliver its log files?

options.text: An Amazon EBS volume attached to one instance
options.rationale: CloudTrail does not write trails to EBS volumes.
Artifact provides AWS compliance reports; it does not store your logs.
Route 53 is a DNS service.
A CloudTrail trail delivers log files to an S3 bucket for long-term storage and analysis.

questions.explanation: Security-related logs such as CloudTrail trails are kept in Amazon S3 (and can also be sent to Amazon CloudWatch Logs) so they can be retained and analyzed.

questions.stem: Which service records the API calls made in an AWS account, including who made each call and when?

options.rationale: CloudTrail logs user activity and API usage across the account for auditing.
CloudWatch collects metrics and logs for monitoring, not an audit trail of API calls.
AWS Config records resource configuration state and changes.
GuardDuty analyzes activity to detect threats; it is not the record of API calls.

questions.explanation: CloudTrail answers who did what, when and from where, which makes it central for auditing and security investigations.

questions.stem: Which service records configuration changes to AWS resources and evaluates them against rules a company defines?

options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls rather than evaluating resource configurations against rules.
AWS Config tracks resource configurations over time and evaluates them against Config rules.
CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.
Trusted Advisor checks against AWS best practices, not custom configuration rules.

questions.explanation: The clue is evaluating configurations against rules: AWS Config records how each resource is configured over time and flags resources that break a Config rule as noncompliant. CloudTrail is the nearest neighbor; it records who made each API call.

questions.stem: Which service collects metrics and logs from AWS resources and can trigger an alarm when a metric crosses a threshold?

options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity for auditing.
AWS Config records configuration changes.
CloudWatch monitors resources and applications with metrics, logs and alarms.
Trusted Advisor checks the account against best practices; it does not collect metrics or set alarms.

questions.explanation: The clue is metrics and alarms: CloudWatch is the monitoring service. CloudTrail is the one people confuse it with; it records API calls for auditing.

questions.stem: Which service uses threat intelligence and machine learning to detect malicious activity in an AWS account, such as unusual API calls?

options.rationale: Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
AWS WAF filters web requests to applications.
GuardDuty continuously monitors accounts and workloads for malicious activity.

questions.explanation: The clue is detecting malicious activity, such as unusual API calls: GuardDuty is the threat detection service. Inspector is the nearest neighbor, but it finds software vulnerabilities, while Shield and WAF block attack traffic.

questions.stem: Which service automatically scans Amazon EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities?

options.rationale: Inspector discovers workloads and scans them for known vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
GuardDuty detects threats from activity, not software vulnerabilities in instances.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service for EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions.

questions.stem: Which service helps protect applications on AWS against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks?

options.rationale: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
AWS Shield is a managed DDoS protection service; Shield Standard is included at no extra charge.
AWS Config records configuration changes.
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity in the account; it does not absorb DDoS traffic.

questions.explanation: The clue is DDoS: AWS Shield is the DDoS protection service, and Shield Standard is applied automatically at no extra charge. GuardDuty detects suspicious activity but does not protect against attack traffic.

questions.stem: Which service gives a central, prioritized view of security findings from services such as Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector and Amazon Macie?

options.rationale: Artifact provides compliance reports.
CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.
Security Hub correlates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and posture-management checks, and prioritizes the most critical issues.
Organizations manages multiple accounts centrally.

questions.explanation: The clue is one central view of findings from several security services: AWS Security Hub brings them together and prioritizes them. CloudWatch also gives a central view, but of metrics and logs, not security findings.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about encryption on AWS are correct? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Encrypting data removes the need for IAM access controls
options.rationale: Encryption complements access control; it does not replace it.

options.text: Customers cannot create or manage their own encryption keys
options.rationale: AWS KMS lets customers create and control keys.

options.text: TLS encrypts data in transit to AWS service endpoints
options.rationale: Encryption in transit commonly uses TLS.

options.text: Encryption in transit is the term for protecting stored data
options.rationale: Protecting stored data is encryption at rest; in transit means data moving over a network.

options.text: Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS support encryption at rest
options.rationale: Storage services support encryption at rest, often with keys from AWS KMS.

questions.explanation: Encryption at rest protects stored data, for example in S3 or EBS; encryption in transit, usually TLS, protects data moving over the network. AWS KMS lets customers create and control the keys.

questions.stem: A security team needs to find out which IAM user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket yesterday. Which service should it check?

options.rationale: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs, not who made API calls.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
CloudTrail records API calls, including who made them and when.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

questions.explanation: CloudTrail event history covers recent management events; a trail keeps them longer in S3.

questions.stem: An auditor wants to see how the configuration of a security group has changed over the past six months. Which service records this configuration history?

options.rationale: CloudWatch tracks metrics, not resource configuration history.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
AWS Config records configuration items over time, giving a history of each resource.

questions.explanation: AWS Config shows what a resource looked like at a point in time and how it changed.

questions.stem: Which service uses machine learning to discover and protect sensitive data, such as personally identifiable information, in Amazon S3?

options.rationale: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and reports on bucket security.
GuardDuty detects threats from activity.
Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities.
Detective helps investigate security findings.

questions.explanation: Macie is the data security service for S3.

questions.stem: A security team wants to find the root cause of a suspicious finding by looking at related account activity over time. Which service is designed for this investigation?

options.rationale: GuardDuty detects threats and creates findings, which Detective then helps investigate.
Detective links related activity from logs into visual summaries so analysts can find the root cause.
Macie finds sensitive data in S3.
AWS Config records resource configuration changes, not a linked view of activity for investigations.

questions.explanation: The clue is investigating the root cause of a finding: Detective analyzes and links related activity so analysts can see what happened. GuardDuty is the nearest neighbor; it detects the threat, and Detective helps investigate it.

questions.stem: Which service creates and controls the encryption keys used to encrypt data across many AWS services?

options.rationale: Secrets Manager stores secrets such as passwords.
Certificate Manager manages TLS certificates.
AWS KMS creates and controls encryption keys, and AWS services such as Amazon S3, Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS use them to encrypt data.
IAM manages identities and permissions.

questions.explanation: KMS keys protect data at rest in services such as S3, EBS and RDS.

questions.stem: A company's compliance rules require its encryption keys to be stored in dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules (HSMs). Which service provides these HSMs?

options.rationale: AWS KMS is a managed key service in which AWS operates the HSMs for you; it suits most needs that do not require HSMs of your own.
Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials.
Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates.
CloudHSM gives you single-tenant HSMs in the AWS Cloud that you control.

questions.explanation: The clue is dedicated, single-tenant HSMs: CloudHSM gives a company its own HSMs. AWS KMS also protects keys with HSMs, but it is a managed service in which AWS operates them.

questions.stem: Which service provisions and manages SSL/TLS certificates used to encrypt data in transit?

options.rationale: ACM provisions, manages and renews public and private certificates.
KMS manages encryption keys, not certificates.
Secrets Manager stores credentials.
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

questions.explanation: The clue is SSL/TLS certificates: ACM creates, stores and renews them for services such as Amazon CloudFront. AWS KMS is the nearest neighbor, but it manages encryption keys, not certificates.

questions.stem: A company must run a workload that needs to meet a specific compliance program. What should it check before choosing services?

options.text: Nothing, because every AWS service meets every program
options.rationale: Compliance scope varies by service.

options.text: Whether each service is in scope for the program
options.rationale: AWS lists which services are in scope for each compliance program.

options.text: That AWS will certify the company's own application
options.rationale: Third-party audits cover AWS's own infrastructure and services; each customer is responsible for demonstrating the compliance of its own workloads.

options.text: That AWS Shield Advanced is turned on
options.rationale: DDoS protection does not establish compliance scope.

questions.explanation: Compliance requirements vary among AWS services; check the services-in-scope list.

questions.stem: Which service centrally configures and manages firewall rules, such as AWS WAF rules, across the accounts in an organization?

options.rationale: AWS WAF holds the web rules themselves; Firewall Manager deploys them across accounts.
Security Hub collects security findings; it does not deploy firewall rules.
Firewall Manager sets up protections such as AWS WAF rules once and applies them across the accounts in AWS Organizations.
IAM Identity Center manages workforce sign-in across accounts, not firewall rules.

questions.explanation: The clue is "centrally across the accounts in an organization": Firewall Manager applies the same protections to many accounts, including new ones as they join. AWS WAF is the nearest neighbor; it holds the rules but does not manage them across accounts.

questions.stem: Which TWO services help a company audit activity and configuration changes in its AWS account? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Amplify builds web and mobile apps.
AWS Config records configuration changes.
Lightsail provides virtual private servers.
CloudTrail records API activity.
Polly converts text to speech.

questions.explanation: CloudTrail answers who did what; Config answers what changed and whether it complies.
